hero.title: Hey, I'm Nicolás
hero.description:
👋 I am a Chilean Industrial and UX/UI Designer based in Hamburg, Germany , with 3 years of experience working on digital projects for the Chilean Government and private organizations.

I have worked on the design of websites, B2B platforms, administration systems, products for managing large amounts of information, and process-oriented platforms. My approach combines usability, interaction design, and information architecture to create clear, intuitive, and efficient digital experiences.

I am particularly interested in designing accessible and inclusive products, following WCAG 2.2 accessibility guidelines and aiming to ensure that interfaces meet Level AA.

vimu.title: VIMU
vimu.description:
ViMu emerged as a response to the gap between museums and potential visitors, identifying a lack of timely information, as well as confusion and scattered information.

The goal of this project was to create a platform that brought together all museums and event information in one place, presenting it clearly and making it easily accessible to users.
vimu.process: ViMu is based on the Double Diamond and Lean UX models, going through multiple phases of divergence and convergence.
vimu.information:
This stage focuses on divergence and information gathering.

The first phase includes desk research to identify or confirm problems. In this case, a decrease of approximately 90% in museum visits was identified following the pandemic.

The second phase consists of interviews with users and stakeholders to understand their pain points, experiences, and expectations.
vimu.insights: The insights were obtained through information saturation from desk research, interviews, and surveys. Key ideas, words, and recurring themes were analyzed and grouped, looking for connections between them. This made it possible to identify quotes, new problems, ways users relate to culture, what they value, essential aspects of the experience, their main motivation for visiting museums, and what makes the difference between interest and attendance.
vimu.museumInsights:
Museums are considered an educational and entertaining way to learn.

A museum is considered interactive when it encourages users to participate in the experience of exploring the museum. Examples include pressing buttons, listening to sounds, movement, screens, etc.

Some users perceive little variety in the content offered by museums and therefore do not consider it necessary to visit again.
vimu.museumEngagement: The number of visits and engagement on posts did not translate into actual museum visits, suggesting that the information was not reaching enough people or was not sufficiently motivating to encourage people to visit the museum.
vimu.userPersona:
The user persona was based on the interviewees' main motivation for visiting museums: "curiosity" and the search for new knowledge.

This also considered the expectations, motivations, and secondary pain points associated with this type of user.
vimu.userJourney:
Since most users learn about museum events through social media, the user journey begins with this discovery.

The user journey consists of discovering an event that has already taken place and searching for an alternative event that satisfies the curiosity sparked by the first one, finding a suitable time, scheduling, purchasing tickets, arriving at the event, and the post-event experience.
vimu.designProcess: The process consisted of brainstorming ideas for this new application, researching references, and defining the application's architecture by combining it with user flows and card sorting; followed by wireframe sketches and low- and high-fidelity prototypes.
vimu.wireframe: This technique allows the application's structure to be visualized quickly and easily. Through sketches, the arrangement of key elements is defined, facilitating the communication of ideas and decision-making during the early stages of development.
vimu.highFidelity:
This stage focused on organizing the information hierarchy and establishing a main focus for the application: discovering new events. Therefore, the home screen focused on presenting events similar to those the user had previously attended, while placing search in the background.

Since plans are not always made in advance and we may not know whether we will feel like going somewhere tomorrow, a nearby events section was added for users who do not have plans yet. Free events, workshops, and activities were also added as additional sections.

A regular monospaced typeface was used based on the concepts of unity, culture, and formality.
A color palette associated with these concepts was used, incorporating knowledge and discovery. This palette was applied using the 30-60-90 rule.

ecorp.title: ECORP
ecorp.subtitle: Robotic avatars for the fire department
ecorp.description:
ECORP is a project that combines virtual reality and robotic avatars in the context of the fire department.

The goal of this project was to create a product that could enable the training of new members while allowing members who no longer have their full capabilities to remain useful to their team.
ecorp.process:
ECORP aims to project a technology into the future and explore a possible use for it. In this case, I chose virtual reality with robotic avatars in a fire department context due to the wide age range and diversity among the members who make up the fire department.

The first step was researching virtual reality technologies, including their development and current applications, in order to move on to benchmarking.
ecorp.information:
This stage focuses on divergence and information gathering.

The first phase includes desk research to identify potential interviews, studies, and publications that could enable the use of virtual reality technology in work environments.
ecorp.benchmarking: It consists of analyzing and comparing industry or competitor standards. In a design project, it helps identify areas for improvement and competitiveness.
ecorp.userPersona: The user persona was based on possible firefighter stereotypes, ranging from experienced firefighters within the department to new recruits.
ecorp.proposal: Based on the references and user personas, a robotic avatar is proposed that can be operated through virtual reality technology. This would allow experienced firefighters who cannot expose themselves to certain dangers to share their field experience with less experienced volunteers.

servel.title: SERVEL
servel.subtitle: SERVEL identified that a significant number of users were experiencing difficulties completing the electoral address change process, but was unable to determine the underlying causes. A UX/UI consultancy was therefore conducted to analyze the user experience and identify the main pain points in the process.
servel.description:
SERVEL identified that a significant number of users were experiencing difficulties completing the electoral address change process, but was unable to determine the underlying causes.

A UX/UI consultancy was conducted to analyze the user experience and identify the main obstacles preventing users from completing the process.

The goal of the consultancy was to identify problems and propose both quick-win improvements and long-term solutions.
servel.process: SERVEL identified that during the electoral address change process, ~37% of users experienced difficulties changing their electoral address and contacted support through one of the available channels.
servel.process2: Following the UX/UI analysis, the questionnaire was identified as the main source of friction. By comparing these findings with the percentage of users who abandoned the process at this stage, it was confirmed that approximately ~70% of all drop-offs occurred in this section.
servel.problemMinor1txt:
1. The SERVEL platform requires users to log in with ClaveÚnica, but this requirement is not communicated in the interface.
2. The website mentions when the process closes but displays the number of days remaining instead of the exact date, leaving users to work it out themselves.
servel.problemMinor2txt: 3. The buttons linking to the SERVEL website and logging out share the same visual style, despite representing entirely different actions.
servel.problemMinor3txt: 4 and 5. Actions with completely opposite purposes share the same visual style.
servel.problemSerious1txt: 6. This was the main issue affecting users. It involved an autocomplete search field that initiated a location search when clicked. The process ended when a location was selected or when the user clicked outside the field. In the latter case, the system treated the location as invalid and redirected users to a manual form that was being phased out.
servel.proposalTxt: Based on the identified issues, solutions were proposed using user experience design principles: a form divided into clearly defined steps, with a small number of related questions at each stage, automatic data saving, and the ability to resume the process later. The proposal also accounted for users accessing the service from anywhere in the country using a desktop computer, laptop, tablet, or mobile phone, including under unstable internet connections.
servel.proposalTxt2:
Several improvements were introduced, including a button with an icon to communicate the requirement for ClaveÚnica, following the Digital Kit guidelines, and displaying the exact date when the process would no longer be available.

Primary buttons, secondary buttons, and critical actions were also identified and visually differentiated. Most importantly, a search confirmation step was introduced, eliminating one of the main friction points identified during the analysis. This helped reduce abandonment by approximately 13% overall and to around 9% at this specific step.

Additionally, the website's government identity was reinforced by applying the design guidelines of the Gob.cl UI Kit.
